project_type: ONOS 2.7.0 optical SDN controller; subproject is the RSA (Routing and Spectrum Assignment) OSGi app at apps/rsa. Pure Java backend. No frontend in this task.
build_system: Bazel via bazelisk, pinned by .bazelversion=3.7.2. NOTE: .bazelrc sets `build --host_force_python=PY2`, so every build MUST override with `--host_force_python=PY3` or the Python host tooling fails. JAVA_HOME must point to OpenJDK 11.
test_framework: osgi_jar_with_tests (JUnit). The rsa app currently ships NO unit tests (apps/rsa/src/test does not exist). Primary verification for this task is: successful .oar build + hotswap into a live ONOS + curl of each endpoint inside the onos-mno-27 pod. If adding JUnit tests, place them under apps/rsa/src/test/java/org/onosproject/rsa/ and they are picked up automatically by osgi_jar_with_tests.
test_command: Build-only verification: `cd /home/manager/build/onos-2.7.0 && JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64 bazelisk build --host_force_python=PY3 //apps/rsa:onos-apps-rsa-oar`. Live verification: hotswap the oar and curl each endpoint (see verification_instructions).
verification_instructions: 1) Build the oar with build_command; artifact lands at /home/manager/build/onos-2.7.0/bazel-bin/apps/rsa/onos-apps-rsa-oar.oar. 2) Hotswap into the onos-mno-27 pod in namespace ai-optical. Because the app is ALREADY ACTIVE, a plain POST activate will NOT replace running code; you must force-reinstall: POD=$(kubectl -n ai-optical get pod -l app=onos-mno-27 -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}'); kubectl -n ai-optical cp <oar> $POD:/tmp/onos-apps-rsa.oar; then DELETE the app (kubectl -n ai-optical exec $POD -- curl -s -u onos:rocks -XDELETE http://localhost:8181/onos/v1/applications/org.onosproject.rsa) and re-POST with activate: kubectl -n ai-optical exec $POD -- curl -s -u onos:rocks -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' --data-binary @/tmp/onos-apps-rsa.oar 'http://localhost:8181/onos/v1/applications?activate=true'; poll /onos/v1/applications/org.onosproject.rsa until state=ACTIVE. 3) curl each endpoint from INSIDE the pod (service is ClusterIP-only, not reachable from cluster host): kubectl -n ai-optical exec deploy/onos-mno-27 -- curl -s -u onos:rocks http://localhost:8181/onos/rsa/<endpoint>. 4) Confirm legacy endpoints still work: POST /onos/rsa/path, GET /onos/rsa/path/{id}, DELETE /onos/rsa/path/{id}. 5) CORS: curl -i with -H 'Origin: http://example.com' and confirm Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is present; send an OPTIONS preflight (curl -i -X OPTIONS -H 'Origin: ...' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: GET') and confirm 200/204 with CORS headers. Reusable helper scripts exist: /home/manager/ai-optical-poc/80-rsa-real/install-rsa-app.sh (idempotent install; note it short-circuits when ACTIVE, so for a CODE update do the force-reinstall above) and run-demo-rsa-real.sh (full closed-loop demo).

key_patterns: Web resources extend org.onosproject.rest.AbstractWebResource and use mapper()/ok()/get(Service.class). JSON is built with Jackson ObjectNode/ArrayNode, camelCase fields. The existing RsaPathWebResource.encodeResult(RsaResult) is the canonical serialization: requestId, blocked, src/dst (ConnectPoint.toString()), startSlot, width, devices[] (deviceId strings), links[] ({src,dst} ConnectPoint strings), ochSignal (via org.onosproject.net.optical.json.OchSignalCodec.encode -> {channelSpacing,gridType,slotGranularity,spacingMultiplier}). JAX-RS Application = RsaWebApplication.getClasses() registers resource+provider classes; this list is scoped to /onos/rsa ONLY, so a CORS ContainerResponseFilter registered here does not affect other ONOS REST APIs. CoreWebApplication registers AuditFilter.class (a ContainerResponseFilter) the exact same way - follow that pattern. SpectrumTable keys links undirected and all mutating/reading methods are `synchronized`; slotCount default 16. RsaManager stores results and intentKeys in ConcurrentHashMap; injects DeviceService; has a SpectrumTable field.
